events.title: The Sun King Dies
events.description: King Louis XIV of France died at Versailles after a reign of 72 years. No other major European monarch has ruled for longer. He had come to the throne as a child, and he left behind a powerful but heavily indebted kingdom.
events.significance: His death closed one of the longest and most influential reigns in European history. It ended an era of French dominance and absolute monarchy.

events.title: Martha, the Last Passenger Pigeon, Dies
events.description: Martha, the last known passenger pigeon, died at the Cincinnati Zoo in Ohio. Her species had once numbered in the billions and darkened North American skies in huge flocks. Hunting and habitat loss wiped it out within decades.
events.significance: Martha's death marked the confirmed extinction of a species driven to extinction by human activity. It became a lasting symbol for the conservation movement.

events.title: The Great Kanto Earthquake
events.description: A massive earthquake struck the Tokyo and Yokohama region on Japan's main island of Honshu. Fires swept through the densely built cities and killed around 100,000 people.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest natural disasters in Japan's history. The rebuilding of Tokyo and Yokohama reshaped both cities and influenced Japanese disaster planning.

events.title: Germany Invades Poland
events.description: German forces under Adolf Hitler invaded Poland at dawn. Britain and France declared war on Germany two days later.
events.significance: The invasion marked the start of World War II in Europe. The war became the deadliest conflict in human history.

events.title: The Wreck of the Titanic Is Found
events.description: A French-American expedition located the wreck of the Titanic on the floor of the North Atlantic. The ship had sunk in 1912 and lay about two and a half miles below the surface.
events.significance: The discovery ended a decades-long search and opened the wreck to study. It renewed worldwide interest in the Titanic story.
